drivingQuestion: Why is one flogged for consecrating an animal blemished from birth?
outcomeNote: Second version of R' Yoḥanan's answer.

segments.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי בַּזְיָא מִילְּתָא, דְּדֶקֶל לֵיכָּא בְּמִינוֹ — לָא לָקֵי, לְאַפּוֹקֵי בַּעַל מוּם, כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא בְּמִינוֹ — לָקֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara presents «an alternative version» of the previous point. Rabbi Yoḥanan «said to» Reish Lakish: «Nevertheless, the matter» of consecrating an animal blemished from the outset «is disgraceful. For» in the case of «a date palm,» as «there is no» item «of its type» that can be sacrificed as an offering, «he is not flogged» for consecrating it. This is «to the exclusion of a blemished» animal; «since there are» items «of its type» that can be sacrificed as offerings, i.e., unblemished animals, «he is flogged» for consecrating it.

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אפילו הכי בזיא מילתא
moves.summary: the species has fit members, so he is flogged
moves.about: a date palm has no sacrificable kind, a blemished animal's kind does, so he is flogged

edges.about: alternative version of R' Yoḥanan's reply: liability because the species has fit members

edges.cueHe: אמר ליה: אפילו הכי בזיא מילתא
edges.about: a date palm has no sacrificable kind, a blemished animal's kind does, so he is flogged

positions.claim: since unblemished animals of its kind are offered, consecrating a blemished one is disgraceful and punishable
